transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Rae Martinez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Head of ML, Acero), Ethan Ross (SRE), Lena Ortiz (Product), Noah Kim (Eng)

Summary (auto): High-level discovery on migrating from OpenAI hosted to Redwood Dedicated. Discussed eval parity, integration surface area, security controls, and required benchmarks.

00:00 Jordan Lee (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate it. we wanna make this efficient — quick intros?
00:10 Maya Patel: Hi Maya here, head of ML at Acero. we run a customer support assistant and clinical triage prompts, mostly on OpenAI right now.
00:18 Ethan Ross: Ethan, we own infra and SRE, interested in networking and security bits.
00:22 Lena Ortiz: Lena, product, i'm focused on rollout plan and metrics (latency, cost).
00:26 Noah Kim: Noah, engineering, deals with inference infra and vLLM experiments.
00:31 Jordan: great thanks. Rae from my side is our systems engineer who does deep dives — Rae, wanna say hi?
00:36 Rae Martinez (SE): hey team, glad to be here. i'll try to keep the technical Qs focused.
00:41 Jordan: quick context: Acero mentioned cost increases and variability on OpenAI and you're evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput + VPC. is that right?
00:50 Maya: yup. we started with OpenAI for speed of dev but costs are spiking and some outputs are drifting; we need more control and predictable latency for SLAs.
00:58 Lena: also governance — need SSO, audit logs, and data residency options.
01:05 Rae: makes sense. can you share current usage patterns? tokens, seq lengths, concurrency?
01:10 Maya: currently about 30M tokens month, 95th seq lengths around 1k for triage flows, lots of short chat turns for support. peak concurrency 60-80 RPS, tail p95 latency target 200-300ms for user-visible flows.
01:28 Jordan: good. and what models are you using on OpenAI?
01:31 Maya: mostly gpt-4o-ish and a few gpt-3.5 for embeddings, we also run a small fleet with Anthropic for some safety checks.
01:40 Rae: okay. so main migration concerns? we've seen customers worry about eval parity — i.e., outputs match what they had on OpenAI — and integration friction when switching runtimes like vLLM or TGI. can you describe your acceptance criteria?
01:55 Maya: top criteria — parity on core prompts (no regression in intent classification or hallucination), latency within 1.5x of current p95 for critical flows, and cost improvement or predictability. security controls must meet our SOC2 requirements.
02:12 Noah: also compatibility — we prototyped vLLM for local experiments, but our code assumes OpenAI API semantics heavily (function calling, role system), so we need Redwood to support those patterns or provide a compatibility layer.
02:26 Rae: Redwood Dedicated supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints and we have SDK shims; function/ tools calling is supported, streaming, and structured outputs. small note: some under-the-hood differences around sampling & tokenizer behavior can cause slight diffs — we recommend eval parity runs to quantify that.
02:45 Ethan: networking — we need VPC peering, private endpoints, and KMS integration. is that possible on Dedicated?
02:52 Jordan: yes Dedicated includes customer VPC options and KMS/HSM integrations. we can provide audit logs and retention controls; i'll share our SOC2 and security pack.
03:02 Maya: great. about eval parity: how do you run it? we can't accept a black box claim.
03:07 Rae: understandable. typical approach: we ingest your canonical prompt set + labeled outputs, run the same prompts against the target model variants on Dedicated (and any Redwood-verified open model variants), then compute matching metrics — exact match, semantic similarity, safety regressions. we also capture tokenization differences and provide a diff report. we can run a small pilot on our infra or in your VPC depending on your requirements.
03:26 Maya: do you support replicating the same sampling seed or temperature? OpenAI doesn't always surface seeds.
03:32 Rae: some infra differences exist — deterministic seeding is tricky across runtimes. we try to control temperature and top-p, adjust for tokenizer differences, and run multiple seeds to estimate variance. that's why we prefer a statistical parity approach rather than expecting 1:1 identical outputs.
03:46 Lena: are there known model variants that customers pick for parity with GPT-4/4o?
03:51 Rae: we publish a model catalog — Redwood-verified profiles map to common hosted models. for GPT-4-level behavior, customers often pick our tuned open or licensed variants; we'll include the catalog link. page can be small mismatch but our Optimize team can propose quantization/latency profiles.
04:07 Jordan: there's also the option of fallbacks — if Dedicated variant drifts on certain prompts we can route critical flows to hosted or a model variant that matches better while you iterate.
04:16 Maya: interesting. we also care about integration with vLLM/TGI — our experiments used vLLM and TGI on internal infra, but ops overhead was high. will Redwood Dedicated let us keep that operational simplicity?
04:28 Rae: Redwood Dedicated is a managed runtime — we handle the serving runtime, batching, KV cache, kernel selection and optimizations. you get the simplicity of a managed endpoint but with dedicated capacity. if you want, we can surface config options similar to vLLM (cache warmup, batch sizes), but we manage the infra.
04:43 Noah: you mentioned KV cache — how do you manage cache warmup for long sequences? we saw cold-start p99s spike.
04:49 Rae: we have continuous batching and prefix caching; for steady-state triage flows we can pre-warm KV cache based on representative traffic. cold-starts are handled with autoscaling policies and burst capacity; we can tune to meet p99 SLOs.
05:05 Ethan: latency: you said p95 200-300ms is our target — do you have benchmark numbers on Dedicated for comparable sequence lengths?
05:12 Rae: depends on model and hardware. for 1k tokens and smaller user turn lengths we can get p95 in the 150-350ms range on A100/H100 setups with batching tuned. i'll share Redwood-verified perf profiles per model.
05:26 Maya: cost: can you give rough delta vs OpenAI hosted? we want committed monthly cost predictability.
05:32 Jordan: generally customers see lower per-token cost at committed Dedicated rates but you pay for reserved capacity; effective cost depends on utilization. we'll include an example spreadsheet with break-even points at different utilization rates.
05:44 Lena: security: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS — how deep is SSO support? we use SAML with Okta.
05:51 Jordan: we support SAML/SSO and RBAC; Dedicated can integrate with your IdP and maintain audit trails. i'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report.
05:59 Maya: good. legal/procurement: what about data residency and logs retention?
06:03 Jordan: Dedicated can be deployed in region-specific clusters, and we can configure retention policies. for Private/on-prem options we can remove telemetry entirely if needed.
06:12 Noah: question about API compatibility — our app uses function calling heavily; will any differences require rework?
06:18 Rae: we expose function-calling semantics in Redwood API that mirror the common OpenAI patterns; in a few edge cases you might need to tweak payload shapes, but SDK shims handle most. we'll provide a migration guide.
06:31 Maya: in terms of pilot scope, we'd want: 1) parity tests on 5 core prompt groups, 2) latency benchmarks at typical concurrency, 3) a short canary rollout for product flows. realistic?
06:42 Jordan: yes. proposed pilot: 4 weeks — week 1 data ingest and onboarding, week 2 eval parity runs, week 3 perf benchmarks and tuning, week 4 canary + regression monitoring.
06:53 Rae: we'll need sample prompts and a small input dataset. also, access to a staging environment or VPC peering for private testing.
07:00 Maya: ok i'll get the sample prompts and a scrubbed data sample. also need to confirm procurement windows — we have quarterly budget reviews, next commit likely Oct.
07:12 Jordan: understood. i'll get pricing to you aligned with that timeline.
07:16 Ethan: one last infra question — If we want on-prem air-gapped later, is there a path?
07:21 Jordan: yes Private on-prem packaging is available for enterprise licensing, usually a separate engagement. we can outline prerequisites in the security doc.
07:29 Lena: any known gotchas moving from TGI or vLLM outputs to Redwood?
07:33 Rae: tokenizer differences and sampling defaults cause the bulk of variations; TGI sometimes returns slightly different role tags and structured outputs need validation. again, eval parity run will surface those gaps.
07:46 Noah: perfect. can you share a sample runbook for the parity tests?
07:50 Rae: yes i'll share a runbook and a checklist — steps, expected metrics (exact match, semantic sim, hallucination rate), and how we compute pass/fail.
08:00 Jordan: wrap up — recap next steps: Jordan share pricing + security deck, Rae share eval runbook and perf profiles, Acero share prompts + scrubbed dataset, schedule benchmark week of 9/14.
08:13 Maya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:16 Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
08:20 (call ends)

Notes: transcription shows occasional mislabels (vLLM transcribed as VLM in a few places); natural disfluencies preserved. Links shared during call: Redwood security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security/acero-pack), Dedicated pricing spreadsheet (link to be shared via email).
questions: What are acceptance criteria for eval parity?
Can Redwood provide exact API compatibility for function calling?
What security controls are available for Dedicated and Private?
references: Redwood Dedicated pricing spreadsheet (to be shared)
